text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian president Algirdas Brazauskas met with the country's diplomats who gathered in Vilnius for an annual meeting.

- The Lithuanian market gains trust both at home and abroad. The demand for government T-bills exceeded the offer more than four times and the whole 30 million litas emission with one year maturity was sold on Monday with average yield of 11.85 percent.
- Lithuanian Finance Minister Rolandas Matiliauskas, who submitted his letter of resignation to the prime minister last Thursday, expects to remain in his post.
- New Economy Minister Vincas Babilius intends to stimulate export and small businesses in the country.
- The head of the central elections commission Zenonas Vaigauskas said that during municipality elections on March 23, some 7,000 to 9,000 candidates will compete for 1,400 posts.
- Russian singer Josif Kobzon gave a concert in Vilnius. Kobzon denied allegations about his contacts with Russia's criminal world.
- Lithuanian food processing companies have in stock 8,300 tons of meat which they cannot sell as it is too expensive.
- Lietuvos Energija produced 11.9 million giga calories (Gkal) of heating energy in 1996, 17 percent less than in 1995.

- The head of the parliament budget and finance comittee Elvyra Kuneviciene says Matiliauskas will stay in his post for a long time. The prosecutor's office is expected to issue a legal opinion on Matiliauskas' credit from Kredito Bankas this week.
- Central bank official Gitanas Nauseda says in an interview that the link between the litas and the dollar will remain at the fixed four-to-one exchange rate until at least 1999.
